questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
The diagram shows a firm’s long-run cost and revenue curves. LRMC LRAC costs, revenue AR MR O AB C D output At which level of output is the firm both allocatively and productively efficient?

options.A: OA B OB C OC D OD

questions.questionText: To prevent a surplus of milk, each milk producer is given a production quota which specifies the volume of milk he is allowed to supply. Initially the quotas are not tradable, but then trade in quotas is allowed. Who would gain or lose when trade in quotas takes place? purchasers of sellers of quotas quotas

options.A: gain gain

questions.questionText: For the purposes of measuring the income effect of a change in the price of a good, what is not held constant?

options.A: consumer preferences

questions.questionText: An actor is paid $100 000 a year. The next best paid job he could get is as a lecturer at $60 000 a year. What are his transfer earnings and his economic rent? transfer earnings economic rent

The table shows the labour market for an economy in four separate years. In which year was there excess demand in the labour market? working population unemployment job vacancies (millions) rate (%) (thousands)
The table shows the levels of output of a good which can be produced with different combinations of labour and capital. capital labour output (number of machines) (number of workers) (units)
The short-run total costs (SRTC) of a firm are given by the formula SRTC = $(10 000 + 5X2) where X is the level of output. What are the firm’s average fixed costs?
What would be most likely to constrain a firm’s ability to grow?

options.A: the increased difficulty faced by the firm in marketing its product
options.B: the increased risks arising from product diversification
options.C: the increasing costs of distributing goods from a given location
options.D: the increased difficulties faced by the management in coordinating production

questions.questionText: Which would be least likely to practise price discrimination?

options.A: a baker

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the cost and revenue curves of a monopoly. AC MC cost, revenue AR O W X Y Z MR output Which movement between levels of output would indicate a wish to change from unit cost minimisation to earning a normal profit?

options.A: W to Y B W to Z C X to W D X to Z

questions.questionText: What will increase the likelihood that the firms in an industry will collude to maximise their joint profits?

options.A: The industry consists of a large number of producers.
options.B: The industry has many differentiated products.
options.C: The industry is characterised by rapid technological change.
options.D: There are significant barriers to prevent new firms entering the industry.

questions.questionText: What would economists agree should be the aim of any health care system?

options.A: to meet all the health care demands of the population
options.B: to provide every patient with the latest and best available treatment
options.D: to secure the maximum health gain from the resources available

questions.questionText: The government of a country decides to increase the proportion of its tax revenue that it obtains from indirect taxes and to reduce the proportion it obtains from income tax. Total tax revenue is left unchanged. What is likely to be the impact on the distribution of income and on work incentives? distribution work of income incentives

options.A: less equal decrease

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the supply and demand curves of a commodity.

options.A: government subsidy causes the supply curve to shift from S to S .

questions.questionText: Which change would directly affect a country’s Human Development Index?

options.A: a change in average hours worked by the labour force
options.B: a change in life expectancy of the population
options.C: a change in the level of carbon dioxide emissions
options.D: a change in the size of the population

questions.questionText: Despite a government budget deficit, a country’s money supply remains unchanged. What could explain this?

options.A: The country has a balance of payments surplus equal to the government budget deficit.
options.B: The country’s foreign exchange rate is fixed.
options.C: The government budget deficit is financed by borrowing from the central bank.
options.D: The government budget deficit is financed by selling government bonds to members of the public.

questions.questionText: In a closed economy, households pay $0.10 in tax on every $1 increase in their gross income, and spend 5/ of every increase in their disposable income. What is the value of the multiplier?

What will be the effect, in the short run, on the price level and on national output of an increase in aggregate demand if firms are working at full capacity? price level national output

options.A: rise rise

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an economy’s aggregate demand and aggregate supply curves. AS price level AD AD O national output What could cause the aggregate demand curve to shift from AD to AD ?
According to Keynesian analysis, what will be the result of a decrease in the money supply?

options.A: The rate of interest will be reduced, thereby reducing the levels of investment and income.
options.B: The rate of interest will be increased, thereby reducing the levels of investment and income.
options.C: The level of income will be increased as a result of a lower rate of interest and a higher level of investment.
options.D: The price level will fall by the same percentage change as the decrease in the money supply.

questions.questionText: What will be the likely effects on interest rates and bond prices of an increase in the demand for money? interest rates bond prices

options.A: fall fall

questions.questionText: A developing country experiences a rapid growth in labour productivity. What is likely to result from this?

options.A: an appreciation of the country’s nominal exchange rate
options.B: an increase in the country’s balance of trade deficit
options.C: an increase in the country’s inflation rate
options.D: an increase in the country’s relative labour costs

questions.questionText: A government currently has a balanced budget. It is considering the possible variations in tax revenue and government expenditure shown. government options tax revenue expenditure W increase increase X increase reduce Y reduce increase Z reduce reduce Which three options have the potential to move the budget into surplus?

options.A: W, X and Y B W, X and Z C W, Y and Z D X, Y and Z

questions.questionText: The diagram shows an economy’s short-run Phillips curve (SRPC). SRPC the rate of change in money wages O unemployment rate What is assumed to remain constant when drawing this curve?

options.A: the average price level

questions.questionText: The economy of a country is simultaneously experiencing a balance of payments deficit, a budget deficit, demand-pull inflation and unemployment. The government decides to cut personal income taxes. What does this suggest is its main macroeconomic objective?

options.A: to improve the balance of payments position
options.C: to reduce the level of unemployment
options.D: to reduce the rate of inflation

questions.questionText: What is not a valid economic argument for developing economies to pursue a policy of import substitution?

options.A: to embark on industrialisation as a basis for export-led growth
options.B: to exploit their relative abundance of labour in order to produce labour intensive manufacturing goods
options.C: to increase the opportunities for exporting goods in which they already have a comparative advantage
options.D: to reduce their dependence on a narrow range of primary products

questions.questionText: Assuming no change in tax rates or tax-free allowances, for which tax would the amount paid in tax become a smaller proportion of taxpayers’ income during a period of wage and price inflation?

options.A: a progressive income tax

questions.questionText: An economy has a flexible exchange rate. It raises interest rates above the level existing in other countries. What will be the likely effect on the level of domestic demand for goods and services and on the demand for the country’s exports? domestic demand export demand
